The ASV writes no English preposition for the possessive לְ: its relation stands inside the genitive *Jehovah’s*, so the preposition and the name share one unit under rule 30’s one-rendering condition, and the construction-supplied copula *is* joins that fused unit exactly as it joins לִפְנֵי -> *was before* there (rules 20, 49). Head on the lexeme-bearing name. Splitting the pair — *is* to the preposition, *Jehovah’s* to the name — is the competing reading, rejected because that split leaves the לְ holding a copula the construction supplies rather than any rendering of its own relation, and because the corpus fuses לְ + the divine name in all six comparable units (EXO.9.29 *is Jehovah’s*, EXO.13.12 *shall be Jehovah’s*, ISA.44.5 *am Jehovah’s*, 1SA.17.47, EXO.12.11, EXO.12.27). Recording it `noncompositional` instead was also available; `aligned` follows EXO.9.29, the closest parallel, and this chapter’s own לִפְנֵי units.
